meta.title: How teach-me turns a lesson.json into one self-contained page
meta.learnerPromise: Trace a lesson from validated data to a single offline HTML file, and know which tool owns each step.
meta.coreMentalModel: A lesson is data, not markup: the schema gates it, the assembler walks it into fixed widgets, and the inliner folds everything into one file that opens from disk with zero network.

learner.targetOutcome: Modify the render pipeline without breaking self-containment
constraints: No external network at view time

sections.heading: The code path: parse, assemble, inline

blocks.md: `rp1 teach-me render` reads a `lesson.json`, validates it, and emits one `lesson.html`. The pipeline is three hops: **parse** (the schema), **assemble** (walk blocks into `<tm-*>` markup), and **inline** (fold the widget bundle, SVG, and styles into a single file).

blocks.title: Quality lives in the tooling
blocks.md: Lessons never hand-author markup. Every block is described as data and rendered by a fixed, accessible-by-construction widget, so a lesson cannot ship broken or inaccessible HTML.

steps.md: `parseLesson` runs first; an invalid lesson short-circuits the pipe **before** any browser launch or asset read.
`assembleLesson` walks the validated model into `<tm-*>` markup and pre-renders diagrams to static SVG.
`getWidgetBundle` resolves the embedded widget JS+CSS — from the compiled binary, or a dev `dist/` fallback.
`inlineDocument` folds the assembled body and the bundle into one self-contained string.

blocks.md: Stepping through a single `render` call shows who hands what to whom.

steps.title: render receives lesson.json
steps.desc: The command reads the file and JSON.parses it; syntax errors are the caller's to own.
annotations: argument is a path to lesson.json

steps.title: parseLesson validates the model
steps.desc: Structural zod validation, then a version-pairing gate. Failure returns Left and writes no artifact.

steps.title: assembler walks blocks
steps.desc: Each block becomes its <tm-*> element; interactive blocks get a JSON island child.

steps.title: pre-render produces static SVG
steps.desc: Mermaid renders offline to a self-contained <svg>; no runtime diagram library is shipped.

steps.title: inliner folds one file
steps.desc: The widget bundle and styles inline into a single <main>; the script runs at the end of <body>.

blocks.title: Render sequence
blocks.source:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as render
    participant S as parseLesson
    participant A as assembler
    participant I as inliner
    R->>S: validate(lesson)
    S-->>R: Right(model)
    R->>A: assemble(model)
    A->>I: body + bundle
    I-->>R: one self-contained html
blocks.alt: render calls parseLesson which returns a validated model, render passes it to the assembler, the assembler hands a body and bundle to the inliner, and the inliner returns one self-contained HTML string.

blocks.md: An interactive widget is inert markup until its element definition runs. Because the widget `<script>` is at the end of `<body>`, each element upgrades only after its JSON island child is parsed.

states.label: Inert markup
states.description: The <tm-*> element and its JSON island exist in the DOM, but no behavior is attached yet.

states.label: Upgrading
states.description: The tail widget script runs; the element's connectedCallback reads its island.

states.label: Hydrated
states.description: Controls are live <button>s; the island has been read and removed.

blocks.title: Hydration states
blocks.source:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Inert
    Inert --> Upgrading: script executes
    Upgrading --> Hydrated: island read
    Hydrated --> [*]
blocks.alt: A widget starts Inert, moves to Upgrading when the tail script executes, then to Hydrated once its JSON island is read, then completes.

blocks.title: One island shape only
blocks.md: An interactive block's JSON island is **exactly** its schema `data` object. Diverging from the schema shape is the single most common way a widget stays inert.

root.question: Does the block need user interaction (stepping, branching, checking an answer)?

terminal.text: Render it server-side as a static <tm-*> child; the element only adds accessibility semantics.

node.question: Is its payload the schema's data object?

terminal.text: Emit a co-located <script type=application/json> island; the widget hydrates from it.
Fix the schema shape first — a mismatched island leaves the widget inert.

sections.heading: Build a lesson step by step

steps.title: Render
steps.md: Run `render lesson.json -o lesson.html`. A schema error exits non-zero and writes **nothing**.

steps.title: Validate
steps.md: Run `validate` to gate self-containment and run a headless `file://` check.

steps.title: Export
steps.md: Run `export lesson.html -o out.html` to re-assert self-containment and emit the standalone file.

terms.def: A co-located <script type=application/json> child carrying a widget's data.
One HTML file with all CSS/JS/SVG inlined and zero external network references.

questions.q: Where does the widget bundle <script> belong?
questions.explanation: A head script upgrades each element before its JSON island child is parsed, leaving interactive widgets inert; the tail placement fixes hydration.

checks.q: What happens to the output file when parseLesson returns Left?
checks.explanation: render writes output only on success, so a parse or version failure leaves no partial artifact behind.

checks.q: Why must rendered diagrams be static SVG?
choices: So the page loads with zero external network
checks.explanation: Pre-rendering to static SVG means no runtime diagram library is shipped and the page opens offline from a file:// URL.

checks.q: What does the self-containment gate check after rendering?
choices: That the file has valid HTML syntax
That the artifact has no external network references
That the lesson has fewer than 100 lines
checks.explanation: The gate re-asserts that the single-file artifact has zero external src/href references, so it works offline from a file:// URL with no network.

glossary.def: The hand-authored data model a lesson is expressed as.
A fixed <tm-*> custom element that renders one block type from data.

misconceptions: A lesson is HTML you write by hand (it is data validated against a schema).
Diagrams need a runtime library in the page (they are pre-rendered to static SVG).
